name: Romania

income_tax.summary: Flat 10% income tax on most income (exceptions for dividends, capital gains, property transfers and gambling); no local personal income tax. Employees pay CAS 25% and CASS 10% of gross; no ceiling for employees given by PwC. Minimum gross salary implied for 2026 is RON 4,050 a month (RON 48,600 / 12, computed from PwC).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Recorded 19% is a derived approximate rate on an income of about EUR 54,000 (about RON 270,000 at an assumed ~5.0 RON/EUR): CAS 25% on a base of 24 minimum salaries (RON 97,200) = RON 24,300, plus CASS 10% of net income = RON 27,000, total RON 51,300 = 19%. At about EUR 130,000 (RON 650,000) CASS is capped at RON 29,160 (10% of 72 minimum salaries), so the total is RON 53,460, about 8%; the recorded 19% with the RON 291,600 cap gives a close figure. Statutory components: Independent activities: 10% on net income (real system or fixed income quota); CAS 25% on a base of the person's choosing, not below 12 minimum gross salaries (RON 48,600) if annual income is 12-24 minimum salaries, or 24 (RON 97,200) if income is 24 or more; CASS 10% on net annual income, capped at 72 minimum salaries (RON 291,600). The recorded cap is the CASS cap; CAS has no separate ceiling stated. Non-salary income (rent, investments) triggers CASS from 6 minimum salaries (RON 24,300).
income_tax.local_tax_note: There are no local taxes on personal income in Romania (PwC).

regimes.name: Digital nomad long-stay visa
regimes.description: Long-stay visa for non-EU remote workers earning at least three times the average gross monthly salary in Romania for the months before applying (and during the stay), employed by or owning a company registered abroad. One source requires the foreign company to be at least three years old, an older news report says one year. Sources conflict on duration and on the tax exemption (one article says exemption from taxes on income earned outside Romania and from social contributions for up to six months within 12 months if the stay does not exceed 183 days). Legal basis cited by one secondary source: Art. 49(1)(f1) of Government Emergency Ordinance 194/2002 on foreigners. The only exemption found on an opened page is PwC's non-taxable item 'salary income obtained from a foreign employer for employment activities rendered abroad', which does not cover work performed in Romania; a secondary source's statement that the holder's foreign income is exempt for up to six months in 12 (stay under 183 days) was not confirmed in a statute, so covers_local_work stays unset.
regimes.duration_note: Not verified: unofficial sources say 12 months renewable once.
